variants.headline: Building job cancelled part-way
variants.sub: The client has abandoned {project}, which {builder} was building.
variants.body:
The building job for {project}, undertaken by {builder}, has been cancelled part-way because {why}. The client has given up the plan. Readers judging {target} should distinguish this cancellation from a completed handover and consider what responsible stewardship means when an undertaking ends with the work unfinished.

The job has stopped short of completion because the client gave up the plan. That is a different ending from a finished building. Readers should keep the unfinished undertaking in the picture, instead of accepting a neat phrase that makes cancellation sound as though there had never been work to do.

The stewardship of {target} should be assessed against the part-way cancellation. This paper records the abandoned plan without treating it as proof of a particular financial settlement or a subsequent use for the unfinished work. Readers deserve a clear story and a straight answer about responsibility.
